$comment: Self-report instruments for the Gate 1 self_report session, TRANSCRIBED VERBATIM from the official source PDFs (see data/SOURCES.md for provenance and licensing). Item wording is not paraphrased. Only typographic glyphs were normalised to ASCII (see ascii_normalization); the WORDS are exact. Modifications applied on top of the verbatim text: (1) time_anchor rewritten to 'since that happened' at load, original kept in time_anchor_original; (2) PCL-5 items tagged with DSM-5 clusters B/C/D/E, PHQ-9/GAD-7 null; (3) reverse_scored_items left empty for the clinician. Loaded by runner/self_report.py.

ascii_normalization.note: Data files are pure ASCII. Words are verbatim; only these glyphs were substituted.

transcription_notes: PCL-5 time anchor in the source form reads 'IN THE LAST MONTH' (NovoPsych PCL-5), NOT 'in the past month' as the brief stated; the verbatim phrase is recorded in pcl5.time_anchor_original.
GAD-7 uses 'Over the last two weeks' (word 'two'); PHQ-9 uses 'Over the last 2 weeks' (digit '2'). Both recorded verbatim per instrument.
PCL-5 item 15 uses British spelling 'behaviour' - transcribed as-is, not corrected.
PHQ-9 item 8 contains a mid-item question mark ('...could have noticed? Or the opposite...') - transcribed as-is.
reverse_scored_comment: EMPTY BY DESIGN. None of PCL-5/PHQ-9/GAD-7 contains a natively reverse-scored item, so acquiescence is uncontrolled. Reverse-worded items or neutral fillers - and the ids to reverse here - MUST be authored by the clinician. Do not auto-generate them. Scoring inverts any item whose id appears in this list (or whose reverse_scored flag is true).

pcl5.source: PTSD Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5); National Center for PTSD (www.ptsd.va.gov); form distributed by NovoPsych
pcl5.instruction_original: Below is a list of problems and complaints that people sometimes have in response to stressful life experiences. How much you have been bothered by that problem IN THE LAST MONTH.
pcl5.clinical_cutoff_note: Provisional PCL-5 cutoff for probable PTSD (commonly 31-33). Used ONLY by the cutoff-leakage check in runner/self_report.py; totals are discarded as a severity DV.

items.text: Repeated, disturbing, and unwanted memories of the stressful experience?
Repeated, disturbing dreams of the stressful experience?
Suddenly feeling or acting as if the stressful experience were actually happening again (as if you were actually back there reliving it)?
Feeling very upset when something reminded you of the stressful experience?
Having strong physical reactions when something reminded you of the stressful experience (for example, heart pounding, trouble breathing, sweating)?
Avoiding memories, thoughts, or feelings related to the stressful experience?
Avoiding external reminders of the stressful experience (for example, people, places, conversations, activities, objects, or situations)?
Trouble remembering important parts of the stressful experience?

Having strong negative beliefs about yourself, other people, or the world (for example, having thoughts such as: I am bad, there is something seriously wrong with me, no one can be trusted, the world is completely dangerous)?
Blaming yourself or someone else for the stressful experience or what happened after it?
Having strong negative feelings such as fear, horror, anger, guilt, or shame?
Loss of interest in activities that you used to enjoy?
Feeling distant or cut off from other people?
Trouble experiencing positive feelings (for example, being unable to feel happiness or have loving feelings for people close to you)?
Irritable behaviour, angry outbursts, or acting aggressively?
Taking too many risks or doing things that could cause you harm?
Being "superalert" or watchful or on guard?
Feeling jumpy or easily startled?
Having difficulty concentrating?
Trouble falling or staying asleep?

phq9.source: Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9); Copyright (c) 1999 Pfizer Inc.
phq9.instruction_original: Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by any of the following problems?

items.text: Little interest or pleasure in doing things
Feeling down, depressed, or hopeless
Trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping too much
Feeling tired or having little energy
Poor appetite or overeating
Feeling bad about yourself - or that you are a failure or have let yourself or your family down
Trouble concentrating on things, such as reading the newspaper or watching television
Moving or speaking so slowly that other people could have noticed? Or the opposite - being so fidgety or restless that you have been moving around a lot more than usual
Thoughts that you would be better off dead or of hurting yourself in some way

gad7.instruction_original: Over the last two weeks, how often have you been bothered by the following problems?

items.text: Feeling nervous, anxious, or on edge
Not being able to stop or control worrying
Worrying too much about different things
Trouble relaxing
Being so restless that it is hard to sit still
Becoming easily annoyed or irritable
Feeling afraid, as if something awful might happen
